carrier.title: Earn from your own trips
carrier.sub: You are flying anyway. The free kilograms in your case are money, not air. Post the route you are taking and receive requests from senders on it.
carrier.ctaSecondary: I need to send a parcel
carrier.stepsTitle: Four steps from a posted trip to money

1.title: Post a trip
1.body: Where from, where to, the date, how many kilograms are free and what you will take. It takes a minute and commits you to nothing.

2.title: Receive requests
2.body: Senders on your route write into the trip's chat. You answer the ones that suit you and decline the rest without explaining yourself.

3.title: Agree and collect
3.body: The terms are fixed as a card in the chat: what you carry, for how much, by when. The handover is photographed, and the photo stays in the record.

4.title: Get paid
4.body: Cash at handover or a transfer — however you agree. The platform takes no part in the settlement and holds no money.

carrier.limitsTitle: What the platform does not do for you
carrier.limitsBody: Vimana is not a carrier and not an insurer. It does not pay on your behalf, does not inspect what is inside a parcel and does not answer for it at customs — the risk of carrying is yours. What it does: puts you in front of senders on your route and keeps a record of the deal showing who handed over what, and when. There are no payments on the platform today.
carrier.closingTitle: You are flying anyway — do not fly empty
carrier.closingBody: Access is by invitation for now, and there is one corridor: UAE ↔ US. Leave an address and we will write when your route opens.

sender.title: Send a parcel with someone who is already flying there
sender.sub: Documents, medicine, a spare part, a present. Not three weeks of freight logistics but a traveller on the date you need — and a record that shows every step.
sender.stepsTitle: Four steps from a request to a confirmed delivery

1.title: Name the route
1.body: Where from, where to, by when. Cities and airports come from a dataset, so there are no codes to memorise.

2.title: Describe the parcel
2.body: What is inside, the weight, the declared value. The value matters: cover is calculated from it, and it is the ceiling in a dispute.

3.title: Choose a carrier
3.body: You can see their activity level, their trust circles and which checks they have passed. A stranger stops being an anonymous name in a chat.

4.title: Confirm receipt
4.body: Photos of the handover and of the delivery go into the record of the deal. They cannot be removed or swapped — any change is detectable.

sender.limitsTitle: What is true here, and what is not yet
sender.limitsBody: The record of a deal cannot be altered unnoticed: the chain stops adding up, and that is checkable independently of us. What does not exist: payments on the platform, escrow and carrier collateral — you settle directly, and the risk of carrying sits with the sender. Vimana is not a courier company; it introduces the two sides and keeps the evidence.
sender.closingTitle: Find the person already flying your route
sender.closingBody: Access is by invitation for now, and there is one corridor: UAE ↔ US. Leave an address and we will write when your direction opens.

business.title: Deliver orders where the usual carriers do not go
business.sub: Closed directions, awkward corridors, deadlines freight logistics cannot meet. Your order travels with a person who is flying anyway — along a route that is not in anybody's tariff table.
business.stepsTitle: How delivery works for a company

1.title: You name the destination
1.body: Country, city, volume and how often. We look at whether that corridor has carriers on it and how frequently they fly.

2.title: The route is made of people
2.body: Not a tariff but particular flights taken by particular people. Where an ordinary service answers "we do not deliver there", this is a question of density rather than of prohibition.

3.title: The carrier answers with a record
3.body: Activity level, passed checks, a history of closed deals. Selecting on those is what you show your own customer.

4.title: Your client receives and confirms
4.body: Photographs of the handover and of the delivery, with the time of each step. That is the proof of delivery you can put in front of somebody.

business.limitsTitle: What works today, and what does not exist yet
business.limitsBody: Working: routes, carrier selection, and a record of the deal with photographs and a verifiable chain. Not built: a business account, invoices, tracking for your customer, an API and volume pricing — none of it can be offered today, and we will not name dates. That is why this page asks for a conversation rather than a signup: describe the route and we will say honestly whether it is solvable now.
business.closingTitle: Tell us where you need to ship
business.closingBody: Leave an address and a line about the destination. We will answer what is possible today and what waits on payments and escrow.

landing.ctaSender: I need to send a parcel
landing.modalTitleBusiness: Tell us where you need to ship
landing.modalSubBusiness: Leave an address and a line about the destination. We will answer what is possible today and what waits on payments and escrow.
landing.heroTitle: Earn from the trips you are already taking
landing.heroSub: Carry parcels along the routes you fly anyway. Post a trip, get requests from senders on it, agree the terms, get paid. And if it is you who needs something delivered — the people who fly are already here.
landing.rulesTitle: Will it be let through the border?
landing.rulesBody: The question that kills a delivery earlier than any other — and the one nobody answers before you are at the desk. We write the rules per corridor, in both directions, with the quotation from the source next to every claim and the date a person last checked it. Free to read.

chain.label: Every event sealed by the hash of the one before it

anchors.label: Chain heads published on servers we do not own

key.label: From "the platform holds your key" to "only you do"

corridor.label: The first corridor. Others follow it

landing.problemTitle: Urgent, fragile and important things do not wait for cargo
landing.problemBody1: Documents, medicine, a part that is not sold in the country, a present for a child. All of it travels with friends of friends through chats of a thousand people, and it works right up to the first disputed case.
landing.problemBody2: It breaks the same way every time: the agreement lived in two people's memory, and when something went wrong there was nothing to point at. We do not replace those people. We give them a record they can point at.
landing.gatesTitle: Four steps, each one leaving a record

post.title: Trip
post.body: The carrier posts a route, a date and the kilograms they have spare. They are flying anyway; the luggage simply is not empty.

match.title: Deal
match.body: The sender finds the trip and offers a parcel. Both sides see each other first: verifications, vouches, past deals. Before agreeing, not after.

handoff.title: Hand-off
handoff.body: A photo and a confirmation at the moment of handing over. The record goes into the chain there and then, not from memory that evening.

release.title: Receipt
release.body: The recipient confirms, the deal closes and is sealed. From then on it can only be read.

landing.evidenceTitle: Three mechanisms instead of three promises

chain.title: The event chain
chain.body: Every entry is sealed by the hash of the one before it, so neither order nor content can change unnoticed: the chain stops adding up.
chain.limit: Detectable, not impossible. Checkable independently of us, as of the date of the last anchor.

identity.title: The key is the identity
identity.body: Your key makes the signatures. Owning it is a ladder: first the platform holds a copy, then you hold one too, then only you do.
identity.limit: While we hold a copy we can sign in your name. Delete it and we cannot.

verification.title: Checks carry dates
verification.body: Identity is confirmed by a document and by people who met the person face to face. Every mark carries the date it was made.
verification.limit: A mark weighs less as it ages: a check from a year ago is not a check from yesterday.

landing.pendingTitle: The list of what we do not do yet
landing.pendingBody: Payment today happens between you directly, in cash or by transfer. Below is what is planned. We name no dates, because we do not have them.

payments.title: Payment on the platform
payments.body: A single payment inside the deal, by card.

escrow.title: Protected cell
escrow.body: The money sits inside the deal: the carrier sees it is there and can take it once receipt is confirmed.

export.title: Deal export
export.body: Download the whole deal and show it to anyone: a lawyer, an insurer. It opens without us.

landing.closingBody: We are opening the first corridor with a small group so that every deal stays in plain sight. Leave your address and we will write once, when it opens.

work.interactionPlaceholder: I answer within a few hours. Send a photo of the parcel and its contents before we agree. I do not carry liquids or anything sealed.

payment.title: How to settle with me
payment.desc: Sent to the other party in the chat when you choose to. Vimana neither checks nor processes these details — you agree between yourselves.
payment.label: Method and details
payment.labelDesc: Cash on handover, a transfer, a wallet — however you prefer to be paid.
payment.placeholder: Cash on handover, or a transfer — I will send the details in the chat.

prefs.title: Region and formats
prefs.hint: Stored on your account, not guessed from the browser.
prefs.weightDesc: Used for trip capacity, parcel weight and the price per unit — on the board, in a deal and in letters.
prefs.datesDesc: Used for departure times, deal events, chat messages and letters. The clock follows the same switch: European is 24-hour, American is 12-hour.
prefs.storageNote: Both switches change only what you see. Weights are stored in kilograms and times in UTC, so the other party reads the same figures in their own format.

rulesIndex.title: Corridor rules
rulesIndex.lede: What it takes to move a thing or an animal across a border. Every statement sits next to a quotation from the rule.
rulesIndex.neverReviewed: Not yet checked against the sources
rulesIndex.emptyBody: The corridors written next are the ones people ask about. Tell us which direction you need.
rulesIndex.failed: Could not load the list. Reload the page: this is not the same as there being nothing here.
rulesIndex.disclaimer: Vimana is not a customs broker and issues none of these documents. Every page states what the sources say and quotes them, so you can check it yourself.
rulesIndex.searchPlaceholder: For example: do I need a permit to take a painting out
rulesIndex.matchedByTitle: The corridor title matched; no individual question did.
rulesIndex.noMatchBody: Try another word, or clear the filters. The directory is still small, and your corridor may simply not be in it yet.
rulesIndex.gapsBody: This directory covers moving animals and works of art between Russia and the United States, and claims nothing beyond that. One US state is worked through; the sanctions layer is not described; and wherever a primary source was unreachable the page says so instead of offering a plausible answer. If your case is not here, ask the responsible authority rather than us.

rulesPage.missingTitle: No rules published for this corridor yet
rulesPage.missingBody: Nothing has been published here. If you need this direction, tell us. The corridors people ask about are the ones written next.
rulesPage.failed: Could not load this page. Try again in a moment.
rulesPage.neverReviewed: Not yet checked against the sources
rulesPage.partiallyTranslated: Some sections are not translated yet and are shown in English. They are marked where they appear.
rulesPage.documentsHint: The figure is days to obtain. Count backwards from the departure date.
rulesPage.disclaimer: Vimana is not a customs broker and issues none of these documents. This page states what the sources say, with the quotation next to each claim, so you can check it yourself. Rules change, and the date above is when a person last compared this text with the source.
rulesPage.questionsTitle: In short: the questions people ask
rulesPage.questionsHint: A short answer, and a link to the section where it is backed by a quotation from the source.
rulesPage.checkedAgo_one: Checked against the source {{count}} day ago
rulesPage.checkedAgo_other: Checked against the source {{count}} days ago
rulesPage.rulesHint: Each section carries the quotation from the rule it rests on.

adminRules.title: Corridor rules
adminRules.description: What a thing needs in order to cross a border. A published rule is a statement the platform makes about somebody else's law, so nothing is published without a cited source, and what people have read is never rewritten — a correction is a new version.
adminRules.loadFailed: Could not load the rule sets
adminRules.actionFailed: The action did not go through
adminRules.pickOne: Pick a set on the left, or create one.
adminRules.newHint: One set is one direction, one jurisdiction and one cargo category. The version number is assigned here.
adminRules.frozenHint: This set is frozen: what people read stays what they read. Publish a new version instead of editing it.
adminRules.sectionsHint: Each section carries its own citation. One without a source cannot be published — the quotation is what makes the claim checkable.
adminRules.noSource: No source yet — this section blocks publication.
adminRules.reqHint: Lead time is the field the checklist counts backwards from the departure date — the one number a person cannot look up for themselves.
adminRules.badJson: The condition is not valid JSON.
adminRules.publishNotePlaceholder: One line for the reader who came back — optional
adminRules.questionsHint: Every answer answers from a section with a citation. A question pointing nowhere blocks publication.
adminRules.answersFromMissing: No such section in this set
adminRules.publishedLive: The page is live for readers and for search engines: it is rendered on request.

adminRoles.title: Roles and offers
adminRoles.description: Offers waiting for an answer. Answered and withdrawn ones live in each account's journal, not here.
adminRoles.empty: Nobody is waiting on an answer.
adminRoles.withdrawReasonPrompt: Why is this offer being withdrawn? It goes into the journal.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: A role gives access to other people's data, so it is proposed rather than assigned: nothing changes for your account until you accept. Every offer, answer and withdrawal is written into a journal.
roles.offeredTitle: You have been offered the role of {{role}}
roles.notYet: Nothing has changed yet. The role starts applying only when you accept it.

what.arbiter: Resolves disputes and, when a party opens it, reads the vault of that deal. Every such read is written into the deal's chain and announced in its chat.
what.compliance_editor: Drafts corridor rules and sends them to review. Publishing a rule is a separate power and is not included.
